definitions: Used to introduce a statement that provides more detailed or accurate information than previously given.
Used to emphasize a statement, especially one that is contrary to what might have been expected or previously stated.
Used to confirm or assert the truth of something.
examples: He said he was busy, but in fact, he was just watching TV.
I thought it would be difficult; in fact, it was quite easy.
She is, in fact, one of the most talented people I know.
